title: The Passport Deadline: Europe vs. Caribbean Citizenship by Investment | Across the Water, Ep. 4
lede: By Nov 12, Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, St Kitts and Nevis and Saint Lucia must tell the European Union whether they will close their citizenship-by-investment programmes by June 2028 or risk losing visa-free travel to Europe. This episode explains how the passport trade works, how much the islands depend on it, Brussels' case and the Caribbean's, and Antigua's offer to close by 2030.
keyPoints: Citizenship-by-investment inflows equalled 34.8% of Dominica's GDP in 2023; across the five states, government CBI revenue averaged 6.5% of GDP in 2019–2023 (IMF).
St Kitts and Nevis's CBI fees fell from 25.8% of GDP in 2022 to 6.0% in 2025, and its fiscal deficit widened to 11.7% of GDP (IMF).
EU Regulation 2025/2441, in force since Dec 30, 2025, makes running an investor citizenship scheme a ground to suspend visa-free access; Vanuatu lost its waiver in 2024 (EUR-Lex, Council of the EU).
The European Commission asked the five states in June to close their programmes by June 1, 2028; formal answers are due Nov 12 (Reuters).
Antigua and Barbuda offered on Oct 30 to close by 2030 if the EU helps replace the revenue; the EU has not said whether it agrees.
